file: papers/pdf/Ross - 2024 - Serendipity - The Role of Chance and Accidents in Creativity.pdf
about: A review arguing that serendipity, the combination of chance and the skill to exploit it, offers a lens on how individual, emotional and environmental factors interact in creativity, and discussing how hard it is to study empirically.

candidates.label: Luck combined with skill
candidates.definition: Serendipity needs both a chance event and the skill to make the most of it. Chance on its own, without the skill to exploit it, is not enough to support creative outcomes.
candidates.applies_when: The account describes an unexpected or lucky event together with the person's ability or effort that turned it to advantage.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Pure luck that the person did nothing to exploit, or a planned, skill-only achievement with no chance element.

candidates.label: Individual, emotional, environmental interplay
candidates.definition: The author presents serendipity as a point where individual, emotional and environmental factors interact to shape the creative process.
candidates.applies_when: The account links a chance-based outcome to a mix of personal traits or skills, emotional states, and features of the person's surroundings.
